newsitem.title: UK: ATHLETICS-BLACK MISSES 400 METRES SOLO SLOT.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-BLACK MISSES 400 METRES SOLO SLOT.

text.p: Double Olympic silver medallist Roger Black, Britain's most successful athlete at the 1996 Atlanta Games, will run only in the 4x400 metres relay at the world athletics championships in Athens next month.
Britain announced their team on Tuesday, leaving 31-year-old Black out of the individual 400 metres event in favour of 24-year-old Jamie Baulch, who also took a 4x400 relay silver medal in Atlanta.

Black, silver medallist in both the 400 and 4x400 at Atlanta, took over from Linford Christie as national team captain last month but was forced to withdraw from the British trials in Birmingham last weekend because of illness.
He intended to compete in Hechtel, Belgium, next weekend and had wanted that race to be taken into consideration.
However, the selectors chose Baulch, who finished third in the trials, for the final 400 metres place with automatic choices Iwan Thomas and Mark Richardson.
